chapters.1.lds: Why does Jesus leave the gathered crowd to visit other towns?
chapters.1.summary: Mark begins with John the Baptist preaching in the desert. Jesus is baptized, and a voice from heaven calls him the beloved Son. He is tested in the desert for forty days. He announces that God’s Kingdom is near and calls four fishermen. In Capernaum he teaches with authority and drives out an unclean spirit. He heals Simon’s mother-in-law and many others at the door. Before dawn he goes out alone to pray. He then leaves for other towns and heals a man with a skin disease.
chapters.2.lds: The selected lesson studies the carriers’ faith and shared help. How does the Sabbath answer connect its purpose with human need?
chapters.2.summary: Four men carry a paralyzed man to Jesus and lower him through the roof. Jesus forgives his sins and heals him. He calls Levi the tax collector and eats with sinners. He is asked why his disciples do not fast. He says no one puts new wine into old wineskins. On a Sabbath his disciples pick grain as they walk. Pharisees object, and he recalls what David did when hungry. He says the Sabbath was made for people.
chapters.3.lds: The selected lesson uses the divided house saying to teach unity. How does the question about saving life expose the opponents’ plan?
chapters.3.summary: Jesus enters a synagogue where a man has a withered hand. His opponents watch to see whether he will heal on the Sabbath. He asks whether the Sabbath is for doing good or harm, saving life or killing. They say nothing, and he heals the man. The Pharisees begin to plot his death. Crowds press on him, and he appoints twelve to be with him. Scribes say he drives out demons by their ruler. He says those who do God’s will are his family.
chapters.4.lds: The selected lesson reads the storm account through peace during trouble. Why does fear remain after the disciples hear explanations and see the storm stop?
chapters.4.summary: Jesus teaches a large crowd from a boat. A farmer sows seed on path, rock, thorns, and good soil. He explains the story to his disciples in private. A lamp is meant to be set on a stand. Seed grows by itself while the farmer sleeps. The Kingdom is like a tiny mustard seed that becomes a large plant. That evening a storm fills the boat while Jesus sleeps. He rebukes the wind, and the disciples are terrified.
chapters.5.lds: Why does Jesus stop to hear the woman while Jairus waits?
chapters.5.summary: Jesus crosses the lake and frees a man held by many demons. The man had lived among tombs, and no chain could hold him. The townspeople beg Jesus to leave. Jairus, a synagogue leader, begs him to come to his dying daughter. On the way a woman who has bled for twelve years touches his cloak. She is healed, and Jesus stops to find her. Word comes that the girl has died. Jesus takes her hand, and she gets up.
chapters.6.lds: What should the disciples have understood from the loaves before the sea encounter?
chapters.6.summary: Jesus teaches in his home town, and the people take offense. He sends the twelve out two by two. Herod has John the Baptist beheaded after a rash promise at a feast. The twelve return, and Jesus takes them aside to rest. A crowd follows, and he feeds five thousand with five loaves and two fish. That night he walks on the sea toward the disciples’ boat. They are terrified, and he gets in with them. People bring the sick wherever he goes.
chapters.7.lds: How can calling property sacred become a refusal to help parents?
chapters.7.summary: Pharisees ask why Jesus’s disciples eat with unwashed hands. He says they honor God with their lips and hold to human tradition. The law says to honor father and mother. They let a man declare his goods “Corban,” a gift to God. He then gives his parents nothing. Jesus says evil comes from within, out of the heart. He heals a foreign woman’s daughter. He opens the ears and mouth of a deaf man.
chapters.8.lds: How does the two-stage healing sit beside Peter’s incomplete understanding?
chapters.8.summary: Jesus feeds four thousand people with seven loaves. Pharisees ask for a sign, and he refuses. In the boat the disciples worry that they have one loaf. He asks whether they still do not understand. At Bethsaida he heals a blind man in two stages. He asks who they say he is, and Peter calls him the Christ. Jesus says he must suffer, and Peter rebukes him. Jesus says his followers must take up their cross.
chapters.9.lds: How does the father’s request differ from the disciples’ silence about their fears?
chapters.9.summary: Jesus is changed in appearance on a mountain before three disciples. A voice from the cloud tells them to listen to him. Below, a father has brought a son whom the disciples could not heal. The father asks Jesus to help if he can. Jesus says all things are possible for one who believes. The father cries that he believes and asks help for his unbelief. Jesus heals the boy and again foretells his death. The disciples argue about who is greatest.
chapters.10.lds: The selected lesson studies the wealthy man’s question about following Jesus. How do the two answers to the same question reveal different desires?
chapters.10.summary: Jesus teaches about marriage and blesses the children. A rich man asks how to inherit eternal life and leaves in sorrow. Jesus foretells his death a third time. James and John ask to sit at his right and left in glory. He says whoever would be great must be a servant. At Jericho a blind beggar named Bartimaeus cries out to him. Jesus asks what he wants. He asks to see, receives his sight, and follows Jesus.
chapters.11.lds: How do the tree scenes frame the temple interruption?
chapters.11.summary: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a colt, and people shout “Hosanna.” The next day he finds a fig tree with leaves and no fruit. He says no one will eat from it again. He drives the buyers and sellers out of the temple. He says God’s house should be a house of prayer for all nations. The following morning the fig tree has withered. He teaches about faith, prayer, and forgiveness. The leaders ask by what authority he does these things.
chapters.12.lds: How does the warning about widows’ houses affect reading the widow’s gift?
chapters.12.summary: Jesus tells of tenants who kill a vineyard owner’s son. He is asked about paying taxes to Caesar and about the resurrection. A scribe asks which commandment is first. Jesus names love of God and love of neighbor. He warns about scribes who love honor and devour widows’ houses. He sits and watches people put money in the temple treasury. Rich people give large sums. A poor widow gives two small coins, all she has.
chapters.13.lds: What work remains possible when the day and hour stay unknown?
chapters.13.summary: A disciple admires the temple’s great stones. Jesus says not one will be left on another. Four disciples ask when this will happen. He warns of deceivers, wars, earthquakes, and trials before councils. They must flee when they see the desolating sacrilege. The Son of Man will come in the clouds. No one knows the day or the hour. They must stay awake, like servants whose master is away.
chapters.14.lds: How does the woman’s action differ from the disciples’ promises?
chapters.14.summary: The leaders look for a way to arrest Jesus. At Bethany a woman pours costly perfume on his head. Some scold her, and Jesus defends her. Judas agrees to betray him. Jesus eats the Passover and gives the bread and the cup. In Gethsemane he prays in anguish while his friends sleep. He is arrested, and all the disciples run. The council condemns him, and Peter denies him three times.
chapters.15.lds: Why does the officer’s recognition follow death rather than escape from the cross?
chapters.15.summary: The council hands Jesus to Pilate. Pilate offers to release him, and the crowd chooses Barabbas. Soldiers dress Jesus in purple and mock him as king. Simon of Cyrene is made to carry his cross. He is crucified with two robbers, and passersby mock him. Darkness covers the land, and he cries out and dies. The temple curtain tears in two. A Roman officer says this man was the Son of God.
chapters.16.lds: The selected lesson teaches resurrection through the Gospel accounts. Why does the tomb message name Peter after his denial?
chapters.16.summary: After the Sabbath three women bring spices to the tomb. They wonder who will roll away the stone. They find it moved and a young man in white inside. He says Jesus has risen and is not there. They must tell his disciples and Peter that he goes ahead to Galilee. The women flee, trembling and afraid. The longer ending tells of Jesus appearing to Mary Magdalene and others. He sends the eleven into all the world.
